extracted.intended_audience: geometers, mathematicians, and students studying classical geometric constructions of conic sections
extracted.subtask_description: Classical geometric procedures and lemmas for constructing conic sections (ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas) from given data: foci/umbilics, vertices, latus rectum, points and tangents. Contains constructive algorithms, auxiliary lemmas, and degenerate-case analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: locating the other umbilicus from given vertex, latus rectum and one umbilicus
rubrics_metrics.description: From a given principal vertex D, latus rectum L, and umbilicus S, the other umbilicus H is given by taking DH to DS in the ratio that the latus rectum is to the difference between the latus rectum and four times DS (i.e. DS:DH :: 4DS - L : L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proportion SP + PH to PH is as 2SP to L; specialized for this corollary with SP = DS gives DS + DH : DH :: 4DS : L, hence DS/DH :: (4DS - L) : L. Use this ratio algebraically or by geometric construction to place H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: determining orbit from velocity at principal vertex
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the body's velocity at the principal vertex D, the orbit is found by taking the latus rectum corresponding to double the distance DS in the duplicate ratio of the given velocity to the circular velocity at distance DS; then DH:DS is given as latus rectum to its difference with 4DS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Corollary 3 of Theorem VIII (earlier) to convert velocity data into an effective latus rectum at doubled distance, then use the ratio to find DH and thereby obtain the conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: composition principle for impulsive perturbations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a body moves in any conic and is given some impulse, the subsequent orbit can be found by composing the body's proper motion with the motion generated by the impulse alone; the resulting combined motion gives the new orbit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the vector (or geometric) sum of the original motion and the impulse-generated motion at the given location; the composite determines the new trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary: continuous perturbations approximated by discrete mutations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a body is continuously disturbed by an external force, the near future course is found approximately by collecting the changes the force induces at certain points and, by analogy with series, estimating continuous variations in intermediate places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample the perturbing force's effect at discrete points, infer a series of small mutations, and interpolate/estimate continuous changes to approximate the new path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XV: tangency condition via two foci and a perpendicular
rubrics_metrics.description: If from two foci (umbilics) S, H of an ellipse or hyperbola two lines SV and HV are drawn to a third point V such that one (HV) equals the transverse axis and the other (SV) is bisected by the perpendicular TR dropped from the perpendicular to HV (i.e. SV bisected at T), then that perpendicular TR touches the conic; conversely, if TR touches the conic then VH equals the axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use equality of TS and TV and equal angles TS T V to conclude bisected angle and hence tangency. Conversely, a tangency implies the stated equalities. This lemma is used to verify tangency of a constructed conic to a given line by checking these equalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XVIII (Prob. X): construct ellipse or hyperbola through a given point tangent to a given line from a given umbilicus and axis length
rubrics_metrics.description: Given common umbilicus S, axis transverse length AB and a point P through which the trajectory must pass, and a line TR that the trajectory must be tangent to, construct the circle centered at P with radius AB - SP for an ellipse (or AB + SP for a hyperbola). Drop perpendicular ST to TR and extend to V so that TV = ST; draw the circle centered at V with radius AB. The intersection H of the two circles (with S) yields the other umbilicus; the conic with foci S and H and the given axis is the required trajectory passing through P and tangent to TR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: choose center P and appropriate radius (AB - SP or AB + SP). Drop perpendicular from S to TR, extend to V to make TV = ST. Draw circles (center P, radius as above) and (center V, same radius AB). Intersection H gives the second umbilicus; the conic determined by S, H, and axis data will pass through P and touch TR (use Lemma XV to check tangency). If multiple points or tangents are given, repeat construction to get same H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XIX (Prob. XI): construct a parabola with given focus, point and tangent
rubrics_metrics.description: Given umbilicus S (focus), point P through which the parabola must pass and tangent TR, take center P and describe circle of radius PS. From S drop perpendicular ST to TR and extend to V so that TV = ST; similarly construct other auxiliary circles if another point or tangent is given. Draw common internal tangent IF of the two circles (or appropriate line through intersections). Drop perpendicular SI to IF, bisect at K, and with axis SK and vertex K describe the parabola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use equalities SK = IK and SP = FP to ensure the conic passes through P, and the equality ST = TV with right angle STR to ensure tangency to TR (apply Lemma XIV Cor.3). The method handles cases with single or multiple auxiliary constraints by constructing corresponding circles and their tangent lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XX (Prob. XII): general construction of conic of given species from a given focus through given points and tangents (cases 1–4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given focus (umbilicus) S and the species of the desired conic (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola), construct the conic passing through supplied points and/or tangent to supplied lines by combining circle constructions, perpendicular drops to tangents, bisectors, and proportions to produce the second umbilicus H and axis. Four cases treated: (1) two points given; (2) two tangents given; (3) one point and one tangent given; (4) tangent and an external point given (with additional similarity constructions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case 1: use the given ratio of axis to umbilic distance to map points via KB:BS, LC:CS etc., construct circles with centers at B and C and tangent line KL; drop perpendiculars to find intersections A and a; building axis through Aa gives the conic. Case 2: drop perpendiculars from S to given tangents, extend to points V and v with TV=ST, bisect Vv to find line for axis construction and build circle with diameter Kk to locate H. Case 3: similar to case 2 but using one tangent and one point to produce a corresponding circle and then derive H. Case 4: more elaborate use of similar triangles to match shape of a given conic apb and map it to desired position via similarity of triangles and equalities of constructed segments. Throughout, the criterion for correctness is matching the species via axis-to-umbilicus-distance ratios and verifying tangency via Lemma XV.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XVI: constructing lines through an unknown fourth point given three points with specified differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Given three points A, B, C and a fourth point Z to be found, when the difference between ZA and ZB (or ZA and ZC etc.) is given (or zero), point Z lies on a hyperbola having A and B as foci and transverse axis equal to the given difference; intersections of such hyperbolas (or special perpendicular bisectors if differences are zero) identify Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the hyperbola loci corresponding to the given linear differences (or perpendicular bisector when equal). For three constraints, intersect the corresponding linear loci pairwise to find Z. Special cases: if two distances equal, Z lies on perpendicular bisector; if all equal, Z is the circumcenter of triangle ABC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXI (Prob. XIII): locating the second umbilicus from given focus, point and tangent
rubrics_metrics.description: Given focus S, point P and tangent TR, drop perpendicular ST and extend to Y so TY = ST. Then YH equals the transverse axis; join SP and HP; the difference between HP and the transverse axis is SP. Repeating with multiple tangents or points yields lines (YH or PH) whose relations (equal axes or given differences) determine the other umbilicus H via earlier lemmas, and then the trajectory follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The method converts each constraint (point or tangent) into a line that either equals the axis or differs from it by a known length; use intersections of these constructed lines and Lemma XVI to locate H. Verify by forming the axis (YH) or computing PH ± SP to match the latus rectum condition for ellipse/hyperbola.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium: expedited construction when three points are given
rubrics_metrics.description: When three points B, C, D are given, construct points E, F on the extensions of BC and CD so that EB:EC = SB:SC and FC:FD = SC:SD. Drop normals from EF and form parallels and proportional segments GA:AS etc.; A and Aa become vertex and axis respectively, determining whether the curve is ellipse/parabola/hyperbola by relative magnitudes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a faster, specialized procedure for the three-point case: compute proportional points on extensions, draw normals and parallels, then deduce axis and latus rectum from constructed ratios. Use the size relation of GA to AS to decide species (ellipse/parabola/hyperbola).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XVII: rectangle-ratio lemma for lines from a point to sides of an inscribed trapezoid
rubrics_metrics.description: If from a point P on a conic section inscribed in some trapezoid ABCD four lines PQ, PR, PS, PT are drawn to the trapezoid sides at given angles, then the rectangle PQ×PR is to rectangle PS×PT in a given ratio (determined by the trapezoid and angles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several cases (parallels among trapezoid sides, non-parallel, arbitrary inclinations) are treated by reducing to cases with parallel lines and using similarity of triangles to derive the stated ratio. Use this proportional relation to relate products of constructed segments and thereby test/guarantee that a chosen point P lies on the same conic family determined by the trapezoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XVIII: converse of rectangle-ratio lemma — tangency criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: If for four lines PQ, PR, PS, PT from P to the trapezoid sides the rectangle PQ×PR is to PS×PT in the required given ratio, then the point P is a tangency point of a conic section inscribed in that trapezoid (i.e., P lies on the conic which is tangent to the trapezoid sides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove by contradiction: if P were not on the conic, another intersection would yield a proportional contradiction via Lemma XVII. Use this as a construction-test: after arranging PQ etc. to satisfy the rectangle ratio, you can assert P is a point of tangency for some inscribed conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary (to Lemma XVIII): criterion using three lines and a square ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: If three lines PQ, PR, PS from a common P to AB, CD, AC satisfy that PQ×PR to PS^2 is a given ratio, then P lies on the conic tangent at the corresponding intersection points A and C (and conversely).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This corollary gives a specialized proportional test involving a square (PS squared) which can be used to locate or verify tangency/contact points on the conic by constructing proportional segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XIX: method to find P so that PQ×PR : PS×PT is a given ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: Given four lines AB, CD, AC, BD in fixed positions, find point P from which four lines PQ, PR, PS, PT drawn to those lines meet the rectangle-ratio PQ×PR : PS×PT in a given ratio. The method reduces to choosing an arbitrary line AH for P, intersecting opposite lines, and solving ratios stepwise to locate P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an arbitrary trial line AH and compute intersecting ratios to deduce PR:PT and then use given ratios PI:PR etc. to find P uniquely. Corollaries: 1) Any tangent to the locus can be derived by choosing a point D on the locus; 2) the full locus of P (as a conic) can be constructed by repeating the process for various D and bisecting parallels as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XX: abscissa-proportion lemma for parallelogram tangency
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram ASPQ (with opposite vertices A and P touching a conic) touches a conic at A and P, and the infinitely produced adjacent sides AQ, AS meet the conic again in B and C, then the abscissas PR and PT (parts of opposite sides cut off by intersections with lines from a fifth point) are in a given ratio; conversely if PR:PT is given, then the constructed point D will be tangent to the conic through the four points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casework shows how to relate PR:PT to ratios of constructed rectangles and hence to test tangency by verifying PR:PT. Use the converse to construct tangency points by setting abscissa ratios appropriately and applying Lemma XVIII to deduce contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollaries to Lemma XX: detecting tangents and uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.description: Cor.1: By choosing a point on BC and cutting PT proportionally a Bt will be the tangent at B. Cor.2: Conversely, if Bt is tangent then corresponding BD, CD meet the conic and the proportionality PR:PT = Pr:Pt holds. Cor.3: Two conic sections cannot meet in more than four points (a uniqueness/degeneracy statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These corollaries give practical construction-tests: to get a tangent at B, choose Pt proportional to Pr; conversely, checking proportional abscissas and diagonals identifies consistency with conic intersection properties and prevents impossible multiple intersections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXI: moving-lines generation of conics (pole-polar motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two infinite moving lines BM, CM (with fixed poles B, C) meet in M and describe a given line MN as M moves, and two other moving lines BD, CD with the same poles and given angles meet in D, then the locus of D is a conic section. Conversely, intersections of moving BD, CD that trace a conic imply the associated M moves on a fixed line MN.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lemma shows how one may generate a conic as the envelope/intersection of moving lines by preserving angle relations; it is constructive: choose fixed N on MN and build corresponding points and parallels to get the required ratios and then apply Lemma XX to deduce that D sweeps a conic. Use the converse to derive loci of poles from conic points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXII (Prob. XIV): construct the conic through five given points
rubrics_metrics.description: Given five points A,B,C,D,P, construct the conic passing through them by selecting any two as poles (B,C), drawing parallels through P to lines through those poles, then from the poles drawing infinite families of lines through D, and finally choosing proportional segments Pt, Pr on PT, PR to find intersection d; as the families vary, d tends to D and therefore the conic through the five points is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two equivalent constructions are given: the first uses poles and proportional abscissa selection (Lemma XX) to locate a point d on the desired curve and then pass to the limit as auxiliary lines vary; the alternative uses rotating legs around poles with given angles and tracking intersections to delineate the conic mechanically. Corollaries: tangents, centers, diameters and latus rectum can be found by the constructions of Lemma XIX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXIII (Prob. XV): construct conic through four points and tangent to a given line
rubrics_metrics.description: Given tangent HB with contact B and three other points C,D,P, build parallelogram BSPQ (with PS∥BH and PQ∥BC). Intersect BD with SP at T and CD with PQ at R; pick proportional points Pr, Pt on PQ and PS, and intersections of lines from poles give d lying on the required conic (per Lemma XX and corollaries). Alternate method uses rotation about poles to trace intersections which produce the curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case 1: algebraico-geometric construction via parallelograms and proportional abscissas; Case 2: mechanical construction with rotating radius lines about poles to locate intersections M,N whose envelope describes the conic. For external tangency cases a slightly different computation of the contact point A using proportional rectangles of mean proportionals is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXIV (Prob. XVI): construct conic through three points and two given tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: Given tangents HI, KL and points B,C,D, intersect associated lines BD and CD with the tangent lines to get H,K and I,L; cut the acta RS in proportions determined by mean proportionals between BH/HD and BK/KD, and between CI/ID and CL/LD; the intersections of RS with the tangents give the contact points A and P; with those contacts the conic is described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct AB and CD intersections, compute mean proportionals to get the required ratios for cutting RS, then demonstrate that those intersection points are contact points by invoking Conic proportionality relations. Once contact points found, use previous constructions to produce the full conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXII: transmutation of figures (mapping construction between 'same-kind' figures)
rubrics_metrics.description: A method to transform any figure HGI into another of the same kind by fixing two parallels AO, BL, drawing a third line AB cutting them and mapping a point G to a new point g by a projective-like affine construction using parallels and proportional segments; tangency and order of analytic curves are preserved under this mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lemma gives a tool to simplify problems by transforming complex figures into simpler ones (e.g., making convergent lines into parallels or a conic into a circle) while preserving tangency and analytic order. To use it, transfer intersections, tangents, and defining lines through the affine mapping and solve in the transformed simpler figure; then invert the transformation to obtain the solution in the original figure. Helpful for reducing higher-order curve tangency problems to circles or lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXV (Prob. XVII): construct conic through two points and three given tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two points and three tangents, transform the configuration by taking the two tangents whose pairwise intersections and a line through the two given points form a parallelogram; in the transformed (simpler) figure the two tangents become parallel and the third tangent becomes parallel to the line through the two points. Compute three contact points c,d,e by constructing lengths hc, ic, ke etc. in specified proportional relations (involving sums of given lines and quadratic relations); map these points back by the inverse of Lemma XX to obtain contact points in the original figure and thereby describe the desired conic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Lemma XX to transform the original problem into one with parallel tangents; in that simpler configuration compute contact points using Conic proportional relations (hc^2 : rectangle ahb, etc.), transfer points back via inverse mapping, and then apply Prop. XIV (the four- or five-point constructions) to recover the conic in the original configuration.
